Teamfighting Basics

Five against five is chaos, but it doesn't have to be. Learn your job in a fight, where to stand, and who to hit.

Everyone has a job

Teamfights look messy, but each champion has a job. Knowing yours is the first step:

TypeJobExamples
Tank / engageStart the fight, absorb damage, lock down enemiesMalphite, Leona
Fighter / bruiserDive into the enemy and threaten their carriesDarius, Vi
MageArea damage and crowd control from a safe rangeOrianna, Ziggs
AssassinWait, then kill one squishy targetZed, Ahri
MarksmanDeal steady damage to whoever is in rangeCaitlyn, Jinx
EnchanterShield, heal and speed up the carriesLulu, Janna

Positioning: front line and back line

The simplest way to think about positioning: tanks and fighters stand in front, damage dealers stand behind them.

  • If you're a carry (marksman or mage), your goal is to deal damage while staying alive. Stand behind your front line and hit whatever is in range. Don't walk forward just to reach a better target.
  • If you're a tank, stand in front and make the enemy deal with you. Use your crowd control on whoever is most dangerous.
  • If you're an assassin, wait at the side of the fight, out of vision, until the enemy uses their important crowd control. Then go in.
Pro tipBefore a fight, find the enemy champions that can reach you (assassins, divers, long-range hooks). Stay just out of their range, and watch for them to use their engage before you step forward.

Who to hit

A common mistake is attacking the closest enemy, which is usually the tank. Hitting a tank with 4000 health while their marksman kills your team is a losing trade. Instead:

  • As a marksman or mage, hit the closest safe target. If the enemy carry is in range without you walking forward, hit them. If not, hit the front line, but don't step into danger to reach the back.
  • As an assassin or diver, go for the enemy carry or the fed champion.
  • As a tank or support, protect your carry. Stopping the enemy diver is often more valuable than starting the fight. This is called peeling.

Waiting for the engage

Fights are often won or lost in the first two seconds. A team that starts a fight with a big crowd control ability (like Malphite's Unstoppable Force or Orianna's Shockwave hitting three enemies) usually wins.

This means patience matters. If your team has a strong engage, wait for it and follow up. If the enemy has one, stay spread out so they can't catch several of you at once, and wait for them to use it before committing.

Common mistakeWalking forward alone before your team is ready. If you get caught, it's 4 against 5 and the fight is lost before it starts.

Flanks and chokepoints

Where you fight matters as much as how:

  • Chokepoints are narrow spaces in the jungle and river. Champions with area damage (Ziggs, Miss Fortune, Orianna) love fighting there because the enemy has to bunch up. If your team relies on area damage, try to fight in tight spaces.
  • Open areas like mid lane favor teams with long-range poke and marksmen who need space to kite.
  • Flanking means attacking from the side or behind instead of head-on. It's powerful for assassins and engage champions, because the enemy carries are suddenly in front.

Before an objective fight, look at the map and ask: where do we want this fight to happen? See Objectives: Dragons, Grubs, Herald and Baron.

After the fight

Winning a fight is only half the work. Use it:

  • Take an objective: a dragon, Baron, a tower, or an inhibitor.
  • Push waves out before recalling.
  • Don't chase too far into enemy territory without vision. Many games are thrown by chasing one enemy into four others.

If you lost the fight, back off, clear waves under your towers, and wait for your team to respawn. Don't fight 3 against 5.

Key takeaways

  • Know your job: tank, fighter, mage, assassin, marksman or enchanter.
  • Carries hit the closest safe target and never step into danger to reach the back line.
  • The first big crowd control often decides the fight. Be patient.
  • Area-damage teams want chokepoints; poke and marksman teams want open space.
  • Turn every won fight into an objective.
